newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end slightly higher in quiet dealing.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end slightly higher in quiet dealing.

text.p: Canadian bonds ended Monday slightly higher across the yield curve in quiet trading one day ahead of the close for Wednesday's Christmas holiday, dealers said.
Trading in Canadian bonds was relatively restrained by the lack of trading interest in all markets.

Despite quiet trading in bonds the money market saw two interventions from the Bank of Canada to reaffirm the upper limit of the central bank's 50 basis point target range for Canada's overnight rate at 3.25 percent, traders said.
The Bank of Canada conducted two rounds of special purchase and resale agreements at 3.25 percent.
Dealers said the central bank intervened at first to stem upward pressure on the overnight rate and then a second time to add some liquidity to the system.
They said the lack of cash in the market drove the overnight rate against the upper limit of the central bank's 50 basis point target range at 3.25 percent.

The Bank of Canada also said on Monday the average yield at this week's auction of C$2.3 billion of 90-day Government of Canada treasury was 2.875 percent, 174-day T-bills was 3.257 percent and and on C$1.1 billion of 361-day T-bills was 3.607 percent.

Canada's 30-year benchmark bond was up C$0.20 at the close at a price of 111.45 for a yield of 7.039 percent, while in the short end, Canada's two-year bond rose C$0.12 to 103.54 to yield 4.087 percent. In the money market, Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill yield ended the day up one basis point at 2.91 percent from Friday's close.
